data.name: Mabrouk
data.gender_notes: Mabrouk is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root m-b-r meaning 'to be fortunate, blessed, or prosperous'. In Islamic context, it is often used as a term of congratulations and praise for a newborn child, acknowledging the blessings of God. The name Mabrouk carries the meaning “Fortunate, blessed” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mabrouk usually hope their child will grow to embody fortunate, blessed and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Mabrouk belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fortunate, blessed.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mabrouk total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

historical_references.reference: Mabrouk Ibn Abi Sufra, a famous traveler and geographer during the Abbasid Caliphate period (750-1258 AD). He is known for his extensive travels covering Asia, Europe, and Africa. Mabrouk's descriptions of various regions and cultures were influential in the Islamic world's understanding of the world outside their borders.

Mabrouk Ibn Al Hassan, a Berber general who led the Maghreb Arabs to several military victories during the early Almohad Caliphate period (1121-1163 AD). His military successes helped establish the Almohad Empire and secure control over much of the Maghreb region.
